fix(express,fastify): apply falsy status codes in reply()

The truthiness guard in reply() is there to skip the status call when no status is
passed, but it also drops codes that were provided and happen to be falsy. NaN and 0
never reach response.status(), so the status set before the handler ran survives and
the exception goes out with a 200. Truthy invalid codes such as -1 or 99 already end
up as a 500, because express and fastify reject them.

Skip the call only when no status is given, so a provided code always reaches the
framework that can validate it.

fix(core): scan pre-registered dynamic imports of lazy modules

A lazily loaded `DynamicModule` whose dynamic metadata carries `imports`
never had those imports scanned, so their providers could not resolve.

`NestContainer#setModule` pre-registers a dynamic module's `imports` via
`addDynamicMetadata` -> `addDynamicModules` -> `addModule` before the
scanner recurses into them. Those modules therefore report
`inserted: false`, and the lazy skip condition treated them as already
loaded, leaving them registered but never scanned or instantiated.

Skip only modules that were actually instantiated, and bind global
providers on every lazy pass: a rescanned module reports
`inserted: false`, so `lazy && moduleInserted` skipped binding `@Global`
providers into it.

Closes #17462

fix(platform-express): address body parser review comments

feat: narrow body parser options to the selected parser

`useBodyParser<Options = NestExpressBodyParserOptions>()` never checked its options argument.
`Options` occurs only inside `Omit<Options, 'verify'>`, a non-inferrable position, so it always
fell back to its default, and that default carries a `[key: string]: unknown` index signature.
`keyof` on it is `string | number`, `Exclude<string | number, 'verify'>` removes nothing, and the
resulting `Pick<T, string | number>` collapses to bare index signatures. Every call therefore
accepted any key, any value type, and even `verify` (the single option the signature claims to
remove, and the one Nest reserves to capture `rawBody`).

Key the options off the `parser` argument instead. `NestExpressBodyParserOptionsMap` maps each
parser to the options object its Express factory accepts, derived from `express` itself so the two
cannot drift, and `NestExpressBodyParserType` is now `keyof` that map. The type parameter is
inferred from `parser`, a real inference site, so `useBodyParser('json', ...)` accepts only
`express.json` options and now rejects typos, wrong value types, options belonging to a different
parser, and `verify`.

This is a types-only change; no emitted JavaScript differs.

`NestExpressBodyParserOptions` is
deprecated rather than removed, and calls that pass no explicit type argument are unaffected.

BREAKING CHANGE: `useBodyParser` now takes the parser type as its first type argument.
Calls that
pass an explicit options type, such as `app.useBodyParser<OptionsUrlencoded>('urlencoded', {...})`, no longer compile.
Drop the type argument and let it be inferred from the parser argument.
fix(microservices): call on processing end hook

fix(common): match string file types containing regex metacharacters

`String#match` coerces a string argument into a RegExp, so a `fileType` such as
`image/svg+xml` or `application/ld+json` was compiled into a pattern that cannot
match the MIME type it was written as, and files were rejected with a message
naming the expected type as the type they already had.

Compare a string `fileType` literally before falling back to the existing regex
match, which partial values like `jpeg` still rely on.
style: format union types
refactor: replace non-null assertions with default values

fix(core): correctly scan providers when overriding a lazy-loaded module

The lazy-load short-circuit in scanner.ts relies on the inserted flag
to skip re-scanning already-loaded modules. NestContainer.replaceModule()
was incorrectly returning inserted: false, causing overridden lazy
modules (via testing module builder) to be skipped entirely and their
providers never scanned. replaceModule() always creates a new module
reference that must be scanned, so it now correctly returns
inserted: true.

fix(microservices): nullify grpcclient on close when tryshutdown fails

In the close() method, if graceful shutdown is enabled and
tryShutdown calls back with an error, the promise rejects and
this.grpcClient = null was skipped, leaving a dangling reference.

Wrapped the shutdown logic in try/finally to guarantee nullification
regardless of success or failure.

fix(core): resolve barrier immediately when target count is zero

A Barrier created with targetCount 0 never settled its promise because
signal() was never called for classes with zero constructor or property
dependencies, leaving one forever-pending promise per zero-dependency
class and tripping async-leak detection (e.g. Vitest detectAsyncLeaks).
Resolve eagerly in the constructor and make signal() idempotent past
the threshold to tolerate over-signaling from error paths.

Closes #17392

fix: package_managers.dependabot.dependabot-missing-cooldown.dependabot-missing-cooldown security vulnerability

Automated security fix generated by OrbisAI Security

fix(fastify): run middleware on routes excluded from global prefix

createMiddlewareFactory re-prefixed every non-prefixed middleware path, so a concrete
route excluded via setGlobalPrefix(prefix, { exclude }) (e.g. /graphql) was rewritten to
${prefix}/<route>. Route-scoped middleware was then registered on the wrong path and never
ran on the excluded route. Guard the re-prefix so only a path that collapsed to the root is
expanded, leaving concrete excluded routes unprefixed.

Follow-up to #14895 / #14894. Preserves the exclude: ['/'] behavior from #13401.
